title: Conversation roster has no unenrollment signal for a channel simply omitted from a roster POST
wanted_capability: A clean corpus-side signal that a producer has stopped covering a channel. `ConversationSourceStore::record_roster` writes the latest observation per channel and never deletes one, so a producer that drops a channel from its allowlist and simply stops listing it leaves the last observation on disk forever. Design section 6 says a channel no enrolled source covers must stop being searchable; the S2 projection can only honor that when the roster reports `is_member: false` or when the operator retires the grant.
missing_primitive: Either a roster verb with replace-set semantics (with a producer-side completeness assertion so a partial roster from a mid-restart producer cannot purge a workspace), or an explicit per-channel retirement record the producer/operator can land.
fallback_used: The S2 conversation transcript adapter treats coverage as ending on `is_member: false` or on the operator removing the conversation-lane grant from config, and otherwise relies on purge-on-reproject for channels absent from the store. The limitation is documented on `ConversationTranscriptAdapter` rather than papered over.
notes: Filed while implementing Slack ingestion S2 (corpus projection and search). The S2 purge gate passes on the signals that do exist; this names the one that does not.
